title: Response fidelity playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal playbook for designing few-shot templates and checks that prioritize response-style fidelity (tone, persona consistency, brevity constraints) without blowing the token budget. Notes are intentionally rough — this is a scratchpad for experiments and hypotheses.

Summary of approach:
- Treat style as a soft constraint with measurable primitives (politeness, directness, verbosity, domain register).
- Build a small library of compact exemplars (3–6 tokens shorter than typical) that demonstrate the target style rather than full context-heavy examples.
- Validate with micro-evals: 10 seed prompts × 5 model runs each; aggregate by simple heuristics (keyword overlap, sentence-length distribution, manual spot checks).

Experiment sketches (do in small batches):
1) Minimal exemplar set (3 examples) focusing only on tone markers: short prompt that highlights phrases to emulate.
   - Template: "You are concise, slightly playful, avoid jargon. Examples: [EX1]{=> output}, [EX2]{=> output}, [EX3]{=> output}. Now respond: [USER_PROMPT]"
   - Hypothesis: fewer tokens but higher signal-to-noise for style.

2) Contrastive few-shot: include one example with the wrong style and label it explicitly (NEGATIVE EXAMPLE).
   - Template: "Below: one bad answer (formal). Then three good answers (friendly). Use friendly tone)"
   - Hypothesis: contrastive negative examples speed convergence to target style for instruction-following models.

3) Implicit framing + rubric anchor: avoid long exemplars, instead provide a 2-line rubric ("Goal: friendly, omit technicalities") and 2 tiny exemplars that show the rubric.

Concrete exemplar candidates (short):
- "Friendly: Sure — here's a quick summary: ..."
- "Direct: Here's the short list: ..."
- "Neutral: In a few words: ..."

Failure modes observed (notes from quick runs):
- Overcorrection: model becomes excessively terse when exemplar brevity emphasized; loses necessary detail.
- Style bleed: when prompts include mixed register examples (one playful, one formal), model averages into a bland middle.
- Token budget blowup: naive few-shot with long examples increases latency/cost without style gains.

Mitigations / heuristics to try: 
- Clamp verbosity by adding explicit token constraints: "Keep answer under 60 words" but pair with a 1-line exemplar to show what 60 words look like.
- Use punctuation cues (em dash, exclamation) sparingly in exemplars to nudge energy without adding tokens.
- If detail is required, append a small slot for "If user asks for detail, provide 3 bullets" — mixes style and functional requirements.

Micro-eval checklist (manual + automated):
- Automated: rough lexical match on tone markers (set of 40 tokens mapped to polite/friendly/direct). Score = fraction of tokens present / length.
- Automated: sentence-length mean and SD compared to exemplar outputs.
- Manual: 10 blind labels (A/B) of outputs for perceived tone fidelity.

Test prompts (quick seeds):
- "Explain Newton's second law in one paragraph for a smart high-schooler."
- "Write a short reply declining a meeting politely but firmly."
- "Summarize the design doc in plain language, no more than 4 bullets."

Open questions / next experiments: 
- Does contrastive negative-example framing help at scale (10k prompts)? Tradeoffs?
- Can we distill style anchors into single-token special tokens via fine-tuning or adapters to reduce prompt cost? (team research idea)
- Is it better to enforce style via post-hoc rewrite step (two-step pipeline) vs inline few-shot anchors? Performance/latency tradeoffs?

Action items (short-term):
- Run batch A: 3 exemplars minimal vs rubric-only on prod-small for 500 prompts. Metric: tone score delta, token cost. Owner: me (Samira). ETA: 2025-11-17.
- Draft a compact exemplar library (10 short exemplars covering Friendly/Direct/Formal/Neutral). Owner: Jonah. ETA: 2025-11-14.
- Open a Linear ticket for automated lexical-tone metric (DEVPROMPT-420).

Notes to self:
- Keep exemplars as short fragments (1–2 sentences) — longer narrative examples drift intent.
- Avoid too many explicit labels ("Good answer / Bad answer") in customer-facing templates; use those only in internal tests.
- Record seed outputs into /datasets/prompt-style-mini for later regression checks.

Related references / links:
- Internal prompt library PR (see linked artifacts).
- Prior style experiments: slack thread above with run logs and sample failures.

Rough logs (scratch):
- 2025-10-28: quick pilot on hosted-api m3-small: contrastive negative example reduced polite tokens by ~0.28 (small n).
- 2025-10-30: rubric-only prompt had better recall for required facts but weaker tone adherence.

That’s it for now — saving as a living scratchpad. Will clean, turn into a short README and add to prompt-library once we have first reproducible micro-eval.

Questions for reviewers: 
- If you run the micro-eval, please paste top 3 failure outputs into this doc and tag me.
- Any compact exemplar ideas that don't use full sentences (emoji? single-word cues?) — curious about nonverbal tokens as style anchors.

-- Samira
